commits.edited_message:
rar5: decode read_var() from whatever lookahead is actually available

read_var() now asks for the full 10-byte lookahead first, since that is
the common case, and falls back to however many bytes are actually
available via __archive_read_ahead()'s avail output parameter when that
fails. It decodes within that smaller window instead of failing
outright, only returning an error once the archive genuinely has no
more bytes or the available bytes are exhausted without a terminator.
No call site needed changes, since read_var() now only fails for
genuine errors.

While here, let the file name and link target length checks use the
full byte capacity of the buffers (MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES) instead of
MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS. Both lengths are byte counts, and the stricter
limit needlessly rejects names that the buffers hold without any
problem.

Fixes #3484

Signed-off-by: Gaurav Jadhav <gaurav.vjadhav01@gmail.com>

rar5: Detect 32 bit size_t overflows

If a parsed value does not fit into 32 bit size_t, treat it as error
instead of truncating.

Also drop the 4x scaling of the fixed name buffers. File names and
link targets are accepted only when they fit MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS bytes,
so sizing the buffers as 4 * MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS merely wastes stack
space in every header parser invocation.

Reported-by: krishna28238-arch <krishna28238-arch@users.noreply.github.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>

coupling: The defect is an out-of-bounds stack write (memcpy into a fixed name buffer) that exists in neither edited commit alone; it appears only when the two are composed. Commit 6be8d87 (read_var lookahead fallback) additionally raises BOTH untrusted-length checks in archive_read_support_format_rar5.c -- the file-name check in process_head_file() and the link-target check in parse_file_extra_redir() -- from MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS-1 (2047) to MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES-1 (8191). Read alone, that commit is correct and benign: at that point in history both destination buffers are still declared as char[MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES] (8192), so the widened check exactly matches the buffer capacity (a 8191-byte name plus the NUL terminator fits; verified: the tree with only this edit accepts a 4000-byte name cleanly). Commit 9067eaa (32-bit size_t overflow detection) additionally shrinks BOTH destination buffers from char[MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES] to char[MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS] (2048). Read on top of the base alone (without the first edit), it is correct and benign: the checks still reject anything over 2047 bytes, so the 2048-byte buffers are an exact fit (verified: the tree with only this edit still rejects a 4000-byte name cleanly). Read on top of the first edit -- the actual history -- the shrink's stated justification (names are limited to MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS bytes) was already invalidated by the earlier commit in different functions 250-450 lines away, so neither commit's diff contains a visible mismatch. Composed, the reader accepts name_size/target_size up to 8191 and memcpy's that many bytes from the archive into a 2048-byte stack array: process_head_file() line 2091 (name) and parse_file_extra_redir() line 1550 (link target) -- a stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of up to ~6KB driven entirely by a well-formed RAR5 header. A correct fix is necessarily non-local: the mismatch is between a check introduced by one commit and a buffer declaration rewritten by the other, and BOTH (name, link-target) sink pairings are crossed the same way (check from 6be8d87, buffer from 9067eaa), so fixing only the file-name pairing (e.g. restoring only that check) still leaves the identical overflow reachable through the EX_REDIR link-target path (see pocs/probe_redir.c, which fires with the name path untouched). Restoring the invariant requires editing code added by both commits: clamp the checks to the buffers, or size the buffers to the checks, consistently at both sites. Original batch: both PoCs are rejected cleanly ('Filename is too long' / 'Link target is too long', rc 0). Single-edit trees (either commit alone): rc 0, clean. Combined tree: ASan stack-buffer-overflow WRITE, rc 134/SIGABRT.

pocs.entry_point: api: same public reading API; reaches parse_file_extra_redir via a file header with an EX_REDIR extra field
